public_rationale: The claim depends on a 'reliable version of the product', which the quoted passage does not define. 'More than customers want to pay' has no threshold either. Without those, the claimed tradeoff cannot be tested. The cited evidence covers current products only. On 2026-10-26, CNBC reported that Anthropic's S-1 showed $2.38 billion in cost of revenue against $16.29 billion in revenue for the period ended June 30, 2026, which implies an 85% gross margin (e1). On 2026-04-04, The Next Web reported that analysts saw a price gap of more than five times between what heavy agent users paid on flat subscriptions and what the same usage would cost at API rates (e2). Neither item measures the cost or price of a 'reliable version', so the claim cannot be scored.
limitations: The gross margin figure covers Anthropic's products company-wide for one period. It does not cover a defined 'reliable' product or any other provider.
The margin figure comes from CNBC's coverage of the S-1, not from the filing itself.
The subscription price gap is an analyst estimate that covers only heavy agent use under flat plans.
